Patient VB — Semantic Residual Time-course

Per-bin data: 58 time bins × 3 conditions × 2 phoneme embeddings (348 rows). Bin 0 = -1000 ms from onset; each bin = 100 ms; range -1000 to +4700 ms.

1. Category accuracy across time

The key metric. Shaded bands show ±1 SD across epochs. Dotted vertical lines mark the peak.

3. All metrics × all conditions

Cosine similarity barely changes across conditions (the retrieval baseline is stable), but word accuracy and category accuracy both show strong condition × time interactions.

4. Δ from normal — when does the semantic subspace matter most?

Red = accuracy loss after projecting out the semantic subspace (residualized − normal). Green = accuracy gained by restricting to semantic subspace alone (sem_only − normal). Deeper red/greener peaks mean the semantic subspace carries more of the decoded structure at that timepoint.

5. Heatmap — conditions × time

Brighter = higher category accuracy. The sem_only row clearly dominates in the post-onset window, while residualized collapses to near-baseline.

Key observations:
  • sem_only dominates post-onset: in both embeddings, the sem_only condition reaches its peak in the 400–2000 ms window — consistent with the semantic window identified in partial RSA (400–800 ms).
  • residualized never recovers: after the semantic subspace is projected out, cat_acc stays flat near 0.12–0.15 across almost all bins — no late "phonological bump" emerges.
  • normal tracks sem_only shape: the temporal profile of normal closely mirrors sem_only (same peak timing), but at lower amplitude. This is exactly what's expected if normal is a mixture that includes the semantic subspace.
